claim: A macrostate represents the global thermodynamic state of a protein defined by physical and (bio)chemical conditions such as temperature, pressure, chemical potential, type, and concentration of solutes or ligands.
source_text: Following the nomenclature introduced by Frauenfelder et al., a macrostate represents the global thermodynamic state of a protein defined by the physical and (bio)chemical conditions, such as temperature, pressure, chemical potential, type, and concentration of solutes or ligands (Frauenfelder et al., 1991).

claim: Conformational states are separated by barriers of several kT and interconvert on the timescale of microseconds to milliseconds.

claim: EPR spectroscopy allows the investigation of protein dynamics across a broad range of timescales (from picoseconds to seconds or longer) with few restrictions on sample conditions.
source_text: In this review, we focus on EPR spectroscopy, which allows the investigation of protein dynamics across a broad range of timescales (from picoseconds to seconds or longer) with few restrictions on sample conditions.

claim: Unpaired electrons are usually depleted during protein expression.
source_text: Since unpaired electrons are usually depleted during protein expression, stable radicals need to be introduced for example via site-directed spin labeling in order to obtain an EPR signal (Torricella et al., 2021; Pierro and Drescher, 2023; Jana et al., 2023).

claim: The CW EPR lineshape is highly sensitive to spin label dynamics on the 100 ps to 100 ns timescale which is strongly influenced by structure and dynamics of the protein.
source_text: The CW EPR lineshape (first derivative of the absorption spectrum) is highly sensitive to spin label dynamics on the 100 ps to 100 ns timescale which is strongly influenced by structure and dynamics of the protein (Hubbell et al., 1996; Campbell et al., 2022; Mchaourab et al., 1996; Fichou et al., 2019; Pierro et al., 2020).

claim: When the selection of fitting parameters during lineshape analysis is ambiguous, statistical analysis becomes necessary to assess the likelihood of one parameter set over another.

claim: Power saturation CW EPR spectroscopy provides information on protein topology and is often combined with spin label scanning.
source_text: Further information on protein topology can be obtained via power saturation CW EPR spectroscopy, which is often combined with spin label scanning. Here, spin labels are introduced to successive sites along a sequence of amino acids and the influence of paramagnetic substances on the saturation behavior is evaluated (Altenbach et al., 1990; Hubbell et al., 2003).

claim: Saturation transfer (ST) EPR extends sensitivity to the timescales of microseconds to milliseconds.
source_text: Saturation transfer (ST) EPR and time-resolved (TR) EPR represent two other methods utilizing continuous microwave radiation, extending sensitivity to the timescales of microseconds to milliseconds (Hyde and Dalton, 1972; Hyde and Thomas, 1973; Schwarz et al., 1990; Rayes et al., 2011)

claim: Four-pulse DEER captures interspin distances ranging from 1.5 to 8.0 nm, and even up to 16.0 nm in fully deuterated samples.
source_text: Four-pulse double electron–electron resonance energy transfer (DEER), also known as pulsed electron–electron double resonance (PELDOR), is a pulsed EPR spectroscopic technique usually performed on frozen solutions, in order to resolve distances between two spin labels at sub-Angstrom resolution. This method captures interspin distances ranging from 1.5 to 8.0 nm, and even up to 16.0 nm in fully deuterated samples (Peter et al., 2022; Jeschke, 2012).
evidence_reasoning: This describes the distance range capabilities of DEER, supported by two citations.

claim: DEER experiments elegantly connect structure and thermodynamics of proteins by resolving the conformational ensemble in probability distance distributions.
source_text: Moreover, DEER experiments elegantly connect structure and thermodynamics of proteins by resolving the conformational ensemble in probability distance distributions (Elgeti and Hubbell, 2021; Evans et al., 2020; Dawidowski and Cafiso, 2013; Wingler et al., 2019).

claim: Model-free analysis of DEER data presents a mathematically ill-posed problem that is typically addressed by Tikhonov regularization.
source_text: Model-free analysis of DEER data presents a mathematically ill-posed problem that is typically addressed by Tikhonov regularization which essentially smooths the distance distribution.

claim: The assumption of equal widths for all distance peaks in Tikhonov regularization is inconsistent with the heterogeneous picture of a conformational state.

claim: Selecting surface-exposed spin labeling sites allows the ensemble of spin label rotamers to remain unaffected when the protein changes conformation.
